posts.author: kiwasabi
posts.post_subject: New to holography; how do I get a good start?
posts.content_md:
Hey all,

I just found this great forum and I'm very glad to be a part of it. Recently I got interested in holography on a whim..now I want to do it! 

How do you recommend I get into it? It seems to me that this book is the best: [http://www.amazon.com/Practical-Hologra ... 425&sr=8-1](http://www.amazon.com/Practical-Holography-Third-Graham-Saxby/dp/0750309121/ref=pd_bbs_sr_1/103-8593282-7983821?ie=UTF8&s=books&qid=1184005425&sr=8-1)

Is there a book you folks would recommend over this one? 

Oh, and I'm also looking for people in the Denver/Boulder area who are interested in holography, if you guys know anybody. 

Thanks in advance for any insight and I look forward to talking to you all.

Adam

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: New to holography; how do I get a good start?
posts.content_md:
This is a great book. You will learn from it as you grow your equipment and skills.

Here is a great kit to start with:

[http://www.holokits.com/holography_kit_1.htm](http://www.holokits.com/holography_kit_1.htm)

I like the JD-4 chemistry but you have to be safe with the dichromates.

IF you want a safer alternative use the JD-2 chemistry.

posts.topic_title: New to holography; how do I get a good start?
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: New to holography; how do I get a good start?
posts.content_md:
> **kiwasabi:** Ok, another question for you guys: I'm a 3D Artist; Is there any good way to bring computer 3d images into holograms? Everything you guys are doing seems to be with lasers and physical objects, but what about digital objects?

Well, Liti Holographics main line of business is making integral holograms from a series of images. what you wuold do is take your 3-D modeling software and output a series of images with the camera moving a few inches in between each one. 

Look Here:

[http://www.liti3d.com/cg_hologram.htm](http://www.liti3d.com/cg_hologram.htm)

I bought one of the high end samples and the work was very nice. Kaveh was not has happy with his but he is a holography perfectionist. He can point out defects that I don't notice right away. I would expect there is a big quality difference for the $150 and the $600 versions.

I had in mind when I answered the kind of CGH described, for example, in [http://www.holokits.com/a-Types_of_Holograms.htm](http://www.holokits.com/a-Types_of_Holograms.htm) where the diffraction pattern is calculated and outputed.

posts.topic_title: New to holography; how do I get a good start?
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: New to holography; how do I get a good start?
posts.content_md: Holography uses a unique diffraction grating or bragg diffraction grating for each image. Volumetric displays don't.
